title: Maximizing the algebraic connectivity of graphs of given order and size: a proof of a conjecture of Kolokolnikov
summary: The algebraic connectivity of a graph $G$ is a well-studied graph invariant that is related to other properties of the graph such as connectivity and expansion. Given $n$ and $m$, $α(n,m)$ is the maximum algebraic connectivity of a graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. In 2015, Kolokolnikov conjectured that $α(n,2n-4)=2$ for $n\geq 4$, and verified this claim computationally for $n \le 12$. In this paper, we prove Kolokolnikov's conjecture.
